intended_object: The map induced on cohomology by an A∞ morphism f, i.e. H(f₁) : H(A) → H(B), viewed as a strict A∞ morphism between the cohomology algebras regarded as A∞ algebras with m₁ = 0, m₂ the induced product and higher operations zero (from the docstring and module documentation).
explanation: The body is f.cohomologyMap.cohomologyStrictHom applied to the proof that cohomologyMap preserves degree. cohomologyMap is Submodule.mapQ of the linear part f₁ restricted to cycles (it sends boundaries to boundaries). It is shown multiplicative because, on cycles, f₁(m₂(a,b)) − m₂(f₁a, f₁b) is a boundary, which follows from the arity-two morphism equation (Keller §3.4). NonUnitalAlgHom.cohomologyStrictHom packages a degree-preserving algebra map between cohomologies as a strict A∞ morphism, via the zero-differential DG algebra structure that is definitionally cohomologyAInfinityAlgebra. The lemma coe_cohomologyStrictHom confirms the underlying map is cohomologyMap. The cohomology A∞ algebra here is H(A) with only its product, not the minimal model with transferred higher operations; the docstring of cohomologyAInfinityAlgebra states this explicitly, so the definition matches what it claims. The setting (any commutative ring R, arbitrary modules) is fully general. Mathlib has no A∞ algebras, so there is no counterpart.
